# Classic and JSON packages

This page is for developers and administrators who meet a package in the JSON format, or wonder whether a site
package should use it. It answers: what the two formats are, what changes and what does not, and what the package
server and the installers expect. The complete specification is
[The JSON package format](../../../bc/6.0/package-json-format.md); this page only places it in the site package
picture.

## Two serializations of one package

A package has one model: name, type, version, dependencies, install items, files. That model can be stored in two
ways:

- **Classic**: `package.xml` and XML documents (`ezcontentclass/class-article.xml`, `ezcontentobject/contentobjects.xml`
  ...). The default, and the format of every package on the package server.
- **JSON**: `package.json` and a `.json` file for every document, each one a JSON envelope around the XML element
  in [JsonML](http://www.jsonml.org/), the lossless mapping of XML to JSON arrays.

Because the JSON mirrors the XML element for element, the kernel turns a JSON document back into the same DOM the
XML would give (`eZPackage::fetchDOMFromFile()`), and every package handler runs unchanged. Everything on
[package.xml reference](package-xml-reference.md) applies to both.

## What differs

| | Classic | JSON |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | `package.xml` | `package.json` |
| Documents | `<name>.xml` | the same name with `.json` |
| Images, templates, extension files, install scripts | as they are | as they are, byte for byte |
| Checksums | MD5 of files in `<files>` only | SHA-256 of every file, in `package.json` |
| Rich text (`ezxmltext`) | XML in the document | kept as an XML string, `["#xml", "..."]` (`[PackageFormatSettings] RawXMLDatatypes[]`) |
| Archive name on export | `<name>-<version>-<release>.ezpkg` | `<name>-<version>-<release>.json.ezpkg` |
| Archive format | gzip compressed tar | the same |
| Schema | the kernel's reader | `share/package/schema/package-v1.json` |
| Largest document read | | `[PackageFormatSettings] MaxDocumentBytes`, 64 MB |

## How the kernel tells them apart

By content, never by file name:

- `eZPackage::definitionFilePath()` takes `package.xml` when there is one, else `package.json`.
- On import, both names are extracted from the top of the archive, so either format imports
  (`eZPackage::importUnaudited()`).
- A document named in the definition by its XML name (`filename="class-article"`) is read from the `.xml` file, or
  from the `.json` file of the same name when there is no XML file.
- The package keeps the format it was stored in (`$package->attribute( 'format' )`, `xml` or `json`); an export
  without a format writes that format.

## Site packages and the package server

- Every package in the 6.0.15 folder of the package server is classic: its 44 archives are named `<name>.ezpkg` and
  none is a `.json.ezpkg`. The source repositories (`se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage`,
  `se7enxweb/cjw_multisite-ezpackage`) keep `package.xml` files.
- The setup wizard, the kickstarter and `exp:install` import through `eZPackage::import()`, so they would take a JSON
  archive as well; the index entry (`url`) only has to point at it.
- A site package's install scripts (`settings/*.php`) are payload files and stay PHP in both formats.

> **Note**
> `ezpm convert` converts the documents as they are (`expPackageJson::convertDirectory()`). An **export** of a
> repository package (`ezpm export`, **Download** in the administration) first writes the definition again through
> the kernel's writer (`exportToArchive()`). Before 6.0.15 that writer left out `<settings>` and the `min-version`
> of `<require>` items, and the export dropped files at the top of the package (the `cjw-*.json` side files);
> from 6.0.15 on all three are kept (see
> [package.xml reference](package-xml-reference.md#what-is-lost-when-the-kernel-writes-a-package)). Building site
> package archives from their source folder is still the reliable way to publish them.

## Converting and validating

From the installation root (`./console ezpm ...` runs the same commands):

```bash
# convert an archive; --to defaults to the other format
php ezpm.php convert mypackage-1.0.0-1.ezpkg mypackage-1.0.0-1.json.ezpkg --to=json

# convert into a new directory
php ezpm.php convert mypackage-1.0.0-1.json.ezpkg /path/to/new-directory --to=xml

# export a repository package in a chosen format
php ezpm.php export mypackage -d /path/to/dir --format=json

# check an archive, a directory or a repository package without importing it
php ezpm.php validate mypackage-1.0.0-1.json.ezpkg
```

`validate` checks the schema, every document as XML, the definition, the documents the items name and the checksums,
and prints `PASS` or `FAIL`. In the administration, **Download as JSON** and **Validate** are on a package's page, and
the package wizard asks which format a new package is kept in.

## Which one to choose

| Situation | Format |
|---|---|
| A site package for the shared package server | classic, like every package there |
| Reviewing content packages in pull requests | JSON reads and diffs better for many people and tools |
| Content written by scripts or AI tools, to be reviewed as drafts | JSON, installed with `ezpm install --as-drafts` |
| A package for an installation older than the JSON format | classic |
